ing: Argentine-style pork sausage, or Italian sausage
st: Take the meat out of the fridge [[1 hour]] before cooking so it is not ice cold. Pat the short ribs and flank steak dry with paper towels.
Light the charcoal in a pile at one side of your grill and let it burn until covered in gray ash, about 30 minutes.
Spread the coals into an even bed on one side, leaving the other side empty. Set the grate about 6 inches above the coals.
Season the short ribs generously with [[1 tbsp]] of the coarse salt on both sides. Place them bone side down on the cooler side of the grill and cover loosely.
Cook the short ribs, turning every 20 minutes, until tender and browned, about 1 hour 15 minutes total. Add a few coals as needed to keep the heat gentle.
Prick the sausages once or twice and put them on the cooler side. Cook for about 25 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Salt the flank steak with the remaining coarse salt. Grill it over the hot coals for about 5 minutes per side for medium, to 145°F (63°C).
Rest all the meat on a board for [[10 minutes]], then slice the ribs between the bones and the flank steak against the grain.
Serve everything hot, passing the chimichurri at the table.
Wash the parsley and dry it very well with a towel, since wet leaves make the sauce watery.
Pick the leaves off the thick stems and chop them finely with a sharp knife.
Mince the garlic as finely as you can.
Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl until the salt dissolves.
Add the parsley, garlic, oregano, and chili flakes to the bowl.
Pour in the vinegar and olive oil and stir until well mixed.
Let the sauce sit for at least [[30 minutes]] so the flavors blend, then taste and add more salt or vinegar if needed.
Spoon over grilled meat. It keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Mix the flour and [[1 tsp]] of the salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter with your fingers until crumbly, then stir in the warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 2 minutes, wrap it, and rest it for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground beef, the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt, cumin, and paprika. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Cool completely.
Stir the chopped eggs and olives into the cooled beef filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough out thin on a floured counter and cut twelve 5-inch circles.
Put about [[2 tbsp]] of filling in the middle of each circle. Fold over, press the edges together, and crimp with a fork or twist the edge.
Place the empanadas on a lined baking sheet and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for about 25 minutes until golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes before eating.
Pound the beef cutlets between sheets of plastic wrap to about 1/4 inch thick. Pat dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs in a shallow dish with the garlic and parsley.
Spread the breadcrumbs on a plate.
Dip each cutlet in the egg mixture, let the extra drip off, then press firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Rest the breaded cutlets on a rack for [[10 minutes]] so the coating sticks.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a breadcrumb sizzles right away.
Fry the cutlets in batches for about 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Do not crowd the pan.
Drain on paper towels and serve right away with lemon wedges.

ing: peeled and cubed, or butternut squash
st: The night before, cover the corn and beans with plenty of cold water and soak overnight. Drain and rinse them well.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the pork and beef cubes and brown them lightly, about 6 minutes.
Add the drained corn and beans, the water, and [[1 tsp]] of the salt. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partly covered for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, paprika, cumin, and the remaining salt. Simmer for another 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans and corn are tender.
Mash a few pumpkin pieces against the pot wall to thicken the stew. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
In a skillet, brown the chorizo slices for 5 minutes, then stir them into the pot.
Simmer 10 more minutes, taste for salt, and serve hot in bowls.
Heat a grill or heavy skillet over medium heat. Keep the heat moderate so the sausages cook through without burning.
Cut each chorizo lengthwise almost all the way through, so it opens flat like a book (butterfly).
Grill the sausages cut side down for 6 minutes, then flip and cook another 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Split the bread rolls open and brush the insides lightly with the olive oil.
Toast the rolls cut side down on the grill for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp.
Rub the toasted bread with the cut side of the garlic clove.
Tuck a sausage into each roll and spoon on plenty of chimichurri.
Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and eat while hot.

ing: one 8 oz thick slice or round
st: Use a slice of provolone about 3/4 inch thick. Set it out for 10 minutes so it loses its chill.
Heat a small cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. You can also use a grill.
Brush the olive oil on both sides of the cheese.
Place the cheese in the hot skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes without moving it, until the bottom is browned and crisp.
Flip carefully with a wide spatula and cook the other side for 2 minutes. It should be soft but not melted into a puddle.
Sprinkle the oregano and chili flakes over the top.
Slide the cheese onto a plate and serve right away with bread and tomato slices, scooping it up while it is stretchy.

ing: from about 10 ears, or thawed frozen
grated, such as mozzarella or queso fresco
soaked in warm water 30 minutes, or foil squares
st: If using dried corn husks, soak them in warm water for [[30 minutes]] until pliable. Fresh husks from the ears work too.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Blend the corn kernels with the milk in a food processor until mostly smooth but still a little textured.
Pour the corn into the pan with the onion. Add the salt and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes until thick like porridge.
Stir in the basil and cheese and cook 2 minutes more, then cool for 10 minutes.
Overlap two husks, spoon [[0.33 cup]] of filling into the center, and fold the sides over. Tie with a strip of husk. Repeat to use all filling.
Set the parcels on a steamer rack over simmering water. Cover and steam for 45 minutes until firm.
Let them rest 5 minutes, then open the husks and eat with a spoon.

ing: one for dough, one for brushing
st: Stir the flour, instant yeast, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the warm milk, one egg, and [[4 tbsp]] of the softened butter. Mix to a dough, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and let it rise for [[1 hour]] until nearly doubled.
Roll the dough into a rectangle about 1/4 inch thick. Spread [[4 tbsp]] of the butter over the surface, fold into thirds like a letter, and chill for 20 minutes.
Roll out again, spread the last [[4 tbsp]] of butter, fold into thirds, and chill another 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out to a large rectangle and cut it into 12 triangles. Roll each triangle from the wide end to the tip and curve into a crescent.
Set the crescents on lined baking sheets, cover, and let rise for [[1 hour]] until puffy.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush the crescents with the beaten second egg.
Bake for 18 minutes until deep golden brown.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] sugar with the water for 2 minutes until syrupy, and brush over the warm pastries for a shiny glaze.

ing: thick, see Dulce de Leche recipe
st: Whisk the cornstarch, flour, and baking powder together in a bowl.
Beat the butter and powdered sugar in another bowl until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then the vanilla.
Add the dry mix and stir gently until a soft dough forms. Wrap and chill for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll the dough 1/4 inch thick on a floured surface and cut 2-inch circles.
Place the circles on lined baking sheets, 1 inch apart. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until set but still pale, not brown.
Cool the cookies completely on a rack, since they are fragile when warm.
Spread about 1 tablespoon of dulce de leche on the flat side of half the cookies and top with the rest.
Roll the sides of each sandwich in the shredded coconut and serve.
Choose a large, wide, heavy pot, because the milk foams up as it heats.
Combine the milk, sugar, and baking soda in the pot and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower the heat so it just bubbles. Stir every few minutes.
Simmer uncovered for about 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring more often as it thickens. It will slowly turn pale tan.
When it turns the color of light caramel and coats the spoon, stir in the vanilla.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes more, stirring constantly, until a drop on a cold plate holds its shape. Watch it closely so it does not scorch.
Pour into a clean jar and cool. It thickens more as it chills.
Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into 1/2 inch cubes. Put them in a pot, cover with cold water, add salt and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but the cubes keep their shape. Add the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Drain very well and spread on a tray. Let the vegetables cool completely, about 20 minutes, or the mayonnaise will turn oily.
If using eggs, boil them in water for 10 minutes until fully firm, cool in cold water, then peel and chop. Fully cooked eggs are safe.
Fold the cooled vegetables and eggs with [[0.5 cup]] mayonnaise and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 30 minutes and serve cold.
nt: Best swap: plain Greek yogurt in place of half the mayonnaise for a lighter, tangier salad.

st: Season the pounded cutlets with salt. Whisk the eggs with the garlic and parsley in one dish and spread the breadcrumbs in another.
Dip each cutlet in egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides so the coating sticks. Rest on a rack for 10 minutes.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat to about 350°F, until a crumb sizzles right away.
Fry the cutlets in batches for 3 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on paper towels. Cook beef to at least 160°F.
Heat the broiler. Lay the cutlets on a baking sheet and top each with a slice of ham, [[0.25 cup]] tomato sauce and mozzarella.
Broil 4 minutes until the cheese is melted and spotted with brown. Serve at once with french fries.
nt: Shallow fried, then broiled with cheese
Best swap: use chicken breast cutlets pounded flat for a milanesa de pollo, with the same timings, or bake the breaded cutlets at 425°F.

st: Stir [[3 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1.25 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Knead 8 minutes then let rise, covered, for 1 hour.
Toss the onion with [[1 tsp]] salt and let sit 15 minutes. Squeeze out the water.
Oil a 12 inch pan. Split the dough into 2 pieces and press the larger into the pan, with a slight overhang.
Cover with the mozzarella slices, leaving 1 inch at the edge. Roll the thinner piece into a circle and lay over the cheese.
Fold the overhang over and pinch to seal. Pile the onions on top and drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] oil. Rest 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Bake 20 to 25 minutes until the crust is golden and the onions are soft with brown edges.
Scatter with oregano and olives and serve in wedges.
nt: Best swap: use provolone or low-moisture mozzarella 1 to 1; add a slice of ham between layers for the classic variant.
